title: Rural MAHA Followers Say Trump Health Policies Haven’t Reached Their Communities
summary: President Donald Trump has championed sprawling health policy changes under the Make America Healthy Again movement, but a KFF-Associated Press survey of rural voters found people aren’t seeing the initiatives reach their communities.

title: Drugs Are Widely Used To Sedate Dementia Patients. Her Sons Wanted To Keep Her Off Them.
summary: Potent sedating medications are often used on agitated people with dementia in long-term care facilities despite federal efforts to discourage their use. A clash over whether to drug a Michigan woman illuminates the wrenching decisions families and guardians face.

title: These 100 Nursing Homes Face Perilous Flood Risk. Minnesota Shows What Can Happen.
summary: Staff raced against rising floodwater to evacuate 36 residents from a nursing home in New Richland, Minnesota. It’s one of 100 facilities KFF Health News identified as facing some of the nation’s worst flood risk.

title: US Poised To Boot Legal Immigrants From Medicaid, Including Refugees and Sex-Trafficking Victims
summary: The Congressional Budget Office estimated 100,000 more immigrants will be uninsured by 2034 because of Medicaid eligibility changes under President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act that take effect Oct. 1. A KFF Health News survey of nine states found many more are at imminent risk of losing health coverage.

title: She Left After Waiting Hours in the Emergency Room. The ER Billed Her Anyway.
summary: Autumn Daniels went to the hospital with a severe migraine. After four hours in the waiting room, she left to try a different facility — but the ER still charged her.

title: Confusion and Angst Follow State’s Early Rollout of Medicaid Work Rules
summary: In most states, people with Medicaid coverage will have to prove they’re working, volunteering, or studying starting Jan. 1. But Montana put the rules into effect early, and they’re sowing uncertainty and anxiety.

title: After Failed Execution, Health Workers Say State’s Rules Flout Medical Ethics
summary: The death penalty is legal in 27 states, and lethal injection is the primary method. That means involving medical professionals to store, test, and inject the drugs. After a botched execution in Tennessee, doctors and nurses there say medical professionals need to be removed from the process completely.

title: Republicans and Democrats Find a Unifying Target: Pharmacy Benefit Managers
summary: Some states have considered barring companies that own a PBM from also owning brick-and-mortar pharmacies, as CVS does. Two states have followed through. A similar proposal at the federal level has gained prominent sponsors, aligning conservative, business-friendly Republicans with Democrats traditionally more open to government regulation.

title: Food Safety Finds a Place Among ‘Kitchen-Table’ Political Issues
summary: Recent outbreaks of foodborne illness and high-profile recalls have made this issue a concern of voters.

title: Journalists Discuss What RFK Jr. Recently Told the Anti-Vaccine Group He Founded
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national and local media recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.
